channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: U.S. military destroys 5 Iranian oil tankers as back-and-forth strikes continue
item.description: The U.S. military destroyed five Iranian oil tankers Tuesday and Iran struck back, targeting U.S. troops in Jordan.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. military destroyed five Iranian oil tankers Tuesday and Iran struck back, targeting U.S. troops in Jordan.

item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with retired General Joseph Votel about the latest attacks and counterattacks from Iran.

item.title: Missouri's redistricting fight in turmoil after two different federal court decisions
item.description: The redistricting that Republicans hoped would help them win a key House seat in Missouri is in limbo after contradictory court rulings.
item.content:encoded: The redistricting that Republicans hoped would help them win a key House seat in Missouri is in limbo after contradictory court rulings.

item.title: Republicans kick off a 'Trumpapalooza' of a midterm convention Wednesday in Texas
item.description: Republicans have never held a midterm convention before. But there's also never been a president like Donald Trump. Billed as a "Trumpapalooza," the unprecedented event kicks of in Dallas Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Republicans have never held a midterm convention before. But there's also never been a president like Donald Trump. Billed as a "Trumpapalooza," the unprecedented event kicks of in Dallas Wednesday.

item.title: Citing the 'Deep State,' Trump overhauls the intelligence community
item.description: The catastrophic 9/11 attacks forced the intelligence community to radically revamp its ways of doing business. Now, critics say, President Trump is dismantling much of what was built since then.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: Molly Riley)

item.title: Ballot seizures seemed impossible. But judges and officials are prepping for them now
item.description: The idea of law enforcement taking possession of ballots in the middle of an active election used to be considered impossible. Now, it's a scenario voting officials — and judges — are training for.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: New York City Mayor Mamdani releases documents related to post-9/11 air quality
item.description: New York City has released 170,000 documents it says show officials knew the air quality around the World Trade Center after 9/11 was dangerous to breathe, but they didn't warn local residents.

item.title: Oregon nonprofit harvests fruit from backyards and parks for people in need
item.description: In the Portland, Oregon, area, a nonprofit harvests edible fruit from thousands of metro trees, shrubs and bushes, and distributes it to people in need.
